newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SEEN IMPORTING 400,000-600,000 T WHEAT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SEEN IMPORTING 400,000-600,000 T WHEAT.

text.p: Poland should import the normal 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes of high-gluten durum wheat in the 1997/98 season and might decide if it needs any further imports only after the harvest ends, the Agriculture Ministry said on Friday.
"We expect the standard imports of some 400,000-600,000 high-gluten grain and I cannot comment on other (types of grain) imports," spokeswoman Malgorzata Ksiazek told Reuters.
"The ministry might decide on whether we need any additional imports after the harvest results are known and after evaluating the situation on the market," she added.
Poland, whose growing season runs from September to August, does not grow some types of high-gluten grains and therefore imports them every year.
Ksiazek said the ministry may try to introduce a grain import quota if a need for such a measure arose after this year's harvest but said such a move was only hypothetical.

She said the recent month-long floods, the worst in centuries, had covered some 130,000 hectares of grain fields, 5,500 hectares of rapeseed fields and more than 9,000 hectares of sugar beets, according to the latest tentative estimates.
July's flooding in Poland submerged a total of 6,600 sq km of land, killed 54 and forced hundreds of thousands out of their homes, causing damage of billions of dollars.
